model_annotation: The plot illustrates the measured ACC (%) for six different methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) across varying Co-occurrence Numbers. The x-axis represents the Co-occurrence Number on a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks labeled at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis represents the ACC (%) on a linear scale, featuring a tick label interval of 5 units ranging from 40 to 65. The "Base" method is represented by a solid black line with circular markers, beginning at roughly 38% at the lowest co-occurrence number, increasing to approximately 43.8% at the third data point, and remaining nearly steady to end at 43.9%. The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, exhibiting a continuous upward trend from approximately 39.8% at the start to 47.6% at the end of the x-axis. The "IKE" method is depicted by a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, rising steadily from roughly 42.8% to 49.4% across the plotted range. The "MEND" method, designated by a solid brown line with diamond markers, starts at roughly 44.4%, climbs to 54.0% by the third data point, and concludes at 56.4%. The "MEMIT" method is illustrated by a solid purple line with pentagon markers, demonstrating an initial sharp increase from about 43.5% to 51.0% between the first two data points, followed by a more gradual rise to finish at 54.6%. Finally, the "ROME" method is displayed as a solid green line with square markers, which consistently increases from an initial value of 51.0% to a peak of 66.0% at the highest co-occurrence number.
